title: Location Tracking via GPS Data
description: Live GPS coordinates transmitted in the data flow can be used to track the child's movements over time, creating a detailed profile of their activities and locations.

title: Identification through Location Patterns
description: Analysis of GPS data patterns can reveal the child's home, school, and regular locations, potentially identifying sensitive personal information about their daily routine.

title: Unauthorized Data Storage and Access
description: The backend may store GPS data indefinitely or share it with third parties without proper consent, creating risks of unauthorized access and misuse of location information.

title: Device Impersonation Risk
description: The child's device could be compromised or impersonated, allowing unauthorized parties to transmit false GPS coordinates to the backend.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Location Data
description: Location data stored in DS1 could be accessed by unauthorized parties without proper access controls, encryption, or authentication mechanisms.
assumptions: Assumes DS1 lacks adequate access controls or encryption for stored data.

title: Data Retention Beyond Necessity
description: Location history may be retained longer than necessary for the stated purpose, violating data minimization principles and potentially exposing users to prolonged privacy risks.
assumptions: Assumes no clear retention policy or automatic deletion mechanism exists.

title: Data Profiling
description: Stored location data can be used to create detailed profiles of user behavior, movements, habits, and routines, potentially leading to discrimination or targeted manipulation.
assumptions: Assumes data can be analyzed and aggregated for profiling purposes.

title: Inability to Delete Location Data
description: Users may not have the ability to request deletion of their location history, violating GDPR right to erasure and other privacy regulations.
assumptions: Assumes no user-controlled deletion mechanism or data retention policy exists.

title: Direct Identification Through Location Data
description: Location data can directly identify individuals and their movements, creating privacy risks when combined with other data or when accessed by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Assumes location data is personally identifiable and can be linked to specific individuals.

title: Location Data Interception During Transit
description: Location pings transmitted from backend to geofencing engine could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, enabling tracking of user movements through network eavesdropping or man-in-the-middle attacks.

title: Location Pattern Linkability
description: Sequential location pings can be linked to identify specific users and reconstruct movement patterns, potentially revealing sensitive information about daily routines, workplace, home, and frequent locations.

title: Unauthorized Location Data Retention
description: Geofencing engine may store location pings longer than necessary for zone detection, creating persistent records of user movements that could be accessed without authorization or used for purposes beyond the original intent.

title: Location Data Misuse for Profiling
description: Geofencing engine could use location data to build user profiles, infer sensitive attributes (health conditions, religious practices, political affiliations), or share data with third parties without explicit consent.

title: Excessive Location Data Collection
description: Backend may collect location pings at higher frequency or for longer periods than necessary for geofencing functionality, creating unnecessary privacy burden and increasing exposure to potential threats.

title: Location Data Leakage via Zone Definitions
description: The Family Account Store shares geofencing zone definitions (home, school, friend's house) that contain sensitive location information. This data leakage could reveal family members' addresses, daily routines, and social connections to unauthorized parties.

title: Identification through Location Pattern Analysis
description: Data in transit contains location-based zone definitions that could be used to identify individuals or infer their relationships. Metadata about the parties (e.g., which zones are associated with which family members) could enable identification or profiling.

title: Inadequate Access Controls at Destination
description: The Geofencing Engine may process and store sensitive location data without adequate access controls, potentially allowing unauthorized access to family members' private location information.

title: Lack of User Control Over Location Data Usage
description: Users may not have sufficient control over how their geofencing zone definitions are used by the Geofencing Engine, including potential secondary uses beyond the intended geofencing functionality.

title: Location tracking via geofencing notifications
description: The geofencing data reveals when and where a child enters/exits zones, enabling tracking of movement patterns and creating a detailed location history that can be linked to specific times and places.

title: Inference of sensitive routines and habits
description: Geofencing patterns can reveal daily routines, home/work locations, school attendance, and other sensitive behavioral information through analysis of entry/exit timing and frequency.

title: Unauthorized interception of location notifications
description: Location notifications transmitted over the data flow could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, exposing real-time or historical movement data.

title: Improper storage or sharing of geofencing data
description: The parent entity (EE1) may store, process, or share the received geofencing data in ways that exceed the original purpose or violate privacy expectations.

title: Parent Identity Usurpation During Registration
description: The parent (EE1) could be impersonated during account registration, allowing an unauthorized party to create a child profile and define geofence zones on behalf of the actual parent.
assumptions: Registration process lacks adequate identity verification

title: Child Profile Data Linkability in Transit
description: Child's personal data (name, DOB, school) transmitted in DF6 could be intercepted and linked with other data sources to identify the child across systems or contexts.
assumptions: Data in transit is not adequately encrypted or protected

title: Child Identification via Stored Profile Data
description: The mobile app backend (P1) stores child's name, DOB, and school information, which can be used to uniquely identify the child, potentially enabling profiling or tracking.
assumptions: Backend stores data in a manner that enables identification

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child Sensitive Data
description: The backend (P1) may disclose the child's sensitive profile information to unauthorized parties, violating privacy expectations and potentially applicable regulations like COPPA or GDPR-K.
assumptions: Backend lacks adequate access controls or data sharing policies

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Child Data Processing
description: Processing of child's personal data (name, DOB, school, geofence zones) may violate child privacy regulations such as COPPA (US) or GDPR-K (EU), requiring parental consent and data minimization.
assumptions: Backend does not implement required consent mechanisms or data protection measures for minors
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty on specific regulatory applicability depends on jurisdiction

title: Disclosure of Sensitive Child Data
description: Backend process shares sensitive child profile and geofence zone data with the family account store, creating risk of unauthorized access to information about minors.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Family Data
description: Data store may be accessed by unauthorized parties, leading to disclosure of account, child profile, and geofence information.

title: Inaccurate or Outdated Geofence Data
description: Stored geofence zone data may become inaccurate or outdated, leading to incorrect location-based services and potential safety risks for children.

title: Data Usurpation for Unauthorized Purposes
description: Stored family account and child profile data may be used for purposes beyond the original intent, such as marketing or profiling without consent.

title: Location Data Linkability
description: Child's location data in transit can be linked to other data sources (e.g., school, home, frequent locations) to create a comprehensive profile of the child's movements and activities, potentially revealing sensitive patterns about their life.

title: Location Data Identifiability
description: Location data can identify the child's specific movements, routines, and whereabouts, making it possible to track and identify the child's identity and daily patterns even without explicit identification.

title: Unauthorized Location Monitoring
description: The parent may access the child's location data without the child's consent or knowledge, potentially violating the child's privacy rights and autonomy over their personal information.

title: Location Data Disclosure
description: The mobile app backend may disclose the child's location data to unauthorized third parties, including advertisers, data brokers, or other entities without proper consent or legal basis.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance
description: Processing of child's location data may violate data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, COPPA) regarding children's data, particularly concerning consent, data minimization, and purpose limitation requirements.

title: Location Data Interception in Transit
description: Location history data transmitted between datastore and backend could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, potentially revealing user movement patterns and sensitive location information.

title: Location Data Linkability
description: Location history data in transit could be linked with other data sources to create detailed user profiles or correlate with other activities, enabling tracking and profiling.

title: Improper Storage of Location Data
description: The backend process may store location history data without adequate access controls or encryption, leading to unauthorized access or data breaches.

title: User Identification Through Location Processing
description: The backend process could use location history data to identify or re-identify users, potentially linking location patterns to specific individuals.

title: Inadequate Access Controls at Datastore
description: The location history datastore may lack proper access controls, allowing unauthorized retrieval of sensitive location data before transmission.

title: Identifiability of Child's Location Data
description: When the parent shares the child's location data with a secondary guardian, the act of sharing itself exposes the child's location information, making the child identifiable through their movement patterns and routine locations.

title: Linkability of Location Data in Transit
description: Location data transmitted between the parent and mobile app backend could be linked with other data sources to create a comprehensive profile of the child's movements and associations.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure by Secondary Guardian
description: The mobile app backend (receiving the data) may store or process the child's location data in ways that could lead to further disclosure to unauthorized parties beyond the intended secondary guardian.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance with Children's Privacy Laws
description: Sharing children's location data with secondary guardians may violate regulations such as GDPR, COPPA, or other children's privacy protections that require explicit consent and data minimization.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location Data
description: The secondary guardian may share or disclose the child's live location data to unauthorized third parties, violating the child's privacy expectations.

title: Misuse of Location Data Beyond Authorization
description: The secondary guardian may use the child's location data for purposes beyond the authorized scope, such as tracking the child's movements without consent or for surveillance.

title: Re-identification of Child from Location Patterns
description: The secondary guardian may be able to identify the child through location patterns, even if the data is anonymized, by correlating location data with known routines or locations.

title: Location Data Linkability During Transit
description: Location data in transit may be intercepted and linked with other data sources, potentially revealing the child's identity or movements to unauthorized parties.

title: Inaccurate or Outdated Location Data Sharing
description: The backend may share location data that is inaccurate, delayed, or outdated, leading to incorrect conclusions about the child's actual location or status.

title: Linkability of Aggregated Analytics Data
description: The advertising/analytics partner may be able to link aggregated usage and engagement data to specific users or devices through cross-referencing with other data sources, potentially compromising user anonymity.

title: Re-identification of Users from Aggregated Data
description: Despite being aggregated, the analytics data may contain sufficient detail (e.g., usage patterns, timing, device information) that allows the partner to re-identify individual users or small groups.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Analytics Data
description: The advertising partner may disclose or share the received analytics data with third parties without proper authorization or beyond the scope of the original agreement.

title: Data Misuse Beyond Agreed Purpose
description: The advertising partner may use the analytics data for purposes beyond funding the app's free tier, such as building user profiles for targeted advertising or selling to other data brokers.

title: Regulatory Non-compliance in Data Processing
description: The advertising partner may process the analytics data in ways that violate privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) regarding data minimization, purpose limitation, or user consent requirements.

title: Location data interception during transmission
description: The child's location data in the SOS/check-in message could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission between the child's device and the mobile app backend, potentially revealing the child's real-time location to third parties.

title: Location data linkability for movement tracking
description: The location data could be linked over time to create a movement pattern of the child, potentially revealing sensitive information about their daily routines, school, home, and other frequent locations.

title: SOS message tampering in transit
description: The manual SOS/check-in message could be altered during transmission, potentially leading to false emergency alerts or missed genuine emergencies.

title: Identification of child's whereabouts
description: The parent receiving the location data can identify the child's precise location and activities, which may reveal sensitive information about the child's movements and daily routine.

title: Unintended use of location data by parent
description: The parent may use the location data beyond the intended purpose of safety monitoring, such as for excessive surveillance or controlling the child's movements.
